title: Light, Lanes, Initials, Boundaries & Selects
description: Gradient-lit tubes, masonry with a tolerance dial, real drop caps, the new overscroll chain value, and a select you can finally style.

drops.title: Drawn With Light
drops.description: Ribbons lit by one moving lamp, shaded with a gradient laid across each segment's own normal.
drops.concept: Codrops built lit tubes with TSL and WebGPU; this rebuilds the look on a plain 2D canvas. The curve is cut into short chunks and each chunk is stroked once with a linear gradient across its local perpendicular, so the Lambert term and specular highlight vary smoothly around the cylinder without a shader — and without one stroke per slice.
drops.source: Mathis Biabiany · Codrops, 'Drawing With Light: Lit GPU Tubes with TSL and WebGPU'

interaction.mouse: Drag anywhere to push the light around the scene.
interaction.click: Switch palette between Neon, Chrome and Ember; tune tubes, thickness, gloss and bloom.
interaction.touch: Drag to move the light; all four sliders work on touch.

drops.title: Lanes, Not Rows
drops.description: Native masonry as display: grid-lanes, with the flow-tolerance dial that decides when packing may break reading order.
drops.concept: Grid Lanes is the masonry proposal that actually shipped: one axis keeps its tracks, the other packs items into whichever lane has room. The genuinely new property is flow-tolerance, which sets how much taller a lane may be before the packer is allowed to skip ahead. Here the same algorithm runs in JS so you can watch cards change lanes as you drag it.
drops.source: OpenReplay · 'CSS Grid Lanes: The New Native Masonry Layout'

interaction.mouse: Drag flow-tolerance, columns and gap; cards animate to their new lanes.
interaction.click: Flip between grid-lanes packing and a plain row-locked grid to see the holes lanes remove.
interaction.touch: All controls are touch-sized; the wall reflows to the columns that fit.

drops.title: Sunken Initials
drops.description: Drop caps with initial-letter instead of a float, plus text-wrap: pretty and hanging punctuation.
drops.concept: initial-letter takes a sink and an optional raise and lets the browser resolve the cap against the real line box, so it survives a change of body size or leading that would break a hand-tuned float. Three specimens show sink-only, raised, and a wrapped variant; a toggle forces the float fallback that Firefox and every mail client still get.
drops.source: Modern CSS · 'CSS Drop Caps with the initial-letter Property'

interaction.mouse: Drag sink and raise to resize the caps across all three specimens at once.
interaction.click: Switch text-wrap between pretty, balance and normal; toggle hanging punctuation and the float fallback.
interaction.touch: Sliders and toggles are touch-friendly; specimens stack to one column.

drops.title: Where Scrolling Stops
drops.description: The new overscroll-behavior: chain value — scroll still hands off to the parent, but the browser's boundary gestures stay off.
drops.concept: Firefox 157 shipped a third value for overscroll-behavior. auto lets momentum run into the page and lets pull-to-refresh or swipe-back fire; contain stops both; chain splits them, keeping the hand-off while suppressing the browser's own boundary actions. Three identical nested scrollers run the three values side by side, with a live readout of which container is actually scrolling, plus the bottom sheet the property exists for.
drops.source: MDN · overscroll-behavior — the chain value shipped in Firefox 157 (14 Sep 2026)

interaction.mouse: Scroll each amber list to its end and watch whether the panel behind it moves.
interaction.click: Switch the bottom sheet's overscroll-behavior and drag its grabber to reposition it.
interaction.touch: Scroll and drag the sheet — this is the value you feel most on a phone.

drops.title: The Select, Unsealed
drops.description: appearance: base-select turns a real <select> into something you can style — picker, icon, checkmark and all.
drops.concept: Customizable select is the component story of 2026: opt in with appearance: base-select and the dropdown leaves the OS layer for the page, while staying a real <select> with native keyboard handling and form semantics. Four pickers style ::picker(select), ::picker-icon and ::checkmark, mirror rich option markup through <selectedcontent>, and animate open with @starting-style plus allow-discrete. Where support is missing they stay plain, working native selects.

interaction.mouse: Open any of the four pickers; the accent one repaints the whole page.
interaction.click: Drag the open-duration slider, toggle spring easing, and move the checkmark to the left.
interaction.touch: Tap to open; type-ahead, arrows, Enter and Escape all still work on a keyboard.
